title: An FPRAS for Common Integer Polymatroid Bases with Binary Capacities
main_claim: Theorem 1.1: there is a single randomized algorithm that, given exact value oracles for two integral polymatroid rank functions with common total rank R encoded in binary, outputs a (1±ε) approximation to the number of common integer bases with probability ≥1−δ. On every execution, its oracle calls and bit operations are bounded by poly(n, ℓ, 1/ε, log 1/δ).

issues.description: The transport, observable-variance and trace-mixing estimates are imported wholesale from the cell-bounded companion [CB], Props 5.2/5.4 and Lemmas 5.5–5.6, rather than reproved. The interface hypotheses are verified in this paper: positivity on all p-subsets, the omission/addition properties, agreement on transversals, and the q-comparison. The constants C_p=p(1+8pq^2) and C_d=8+32pq^3 match the companion's transport.tex. So the proof is correct only if CB is.
issues.evidence: counting.tex: 'These are [CB, Propositions 5.2 and 5.4 and Lemmas 5.5--5.6], with q left as the comparison parameter'; CB transport.tex lines 324 and 434 give the same constants.

coverage:
I read every section in full: polyhedra, signatures, geometry, ports, evaluation and counting. Checks made:
- Polyhedral controls: TU uncrossing, the distance bound ≤ n·b, and integer slopes of φ.
- Center lemma.
- Rank-factor parallel-class signature and the balanced-summation induction.
- Encoding in shift-log-concavity (w1−w2 = d0+t(e_j−e_k) at balance).
- Shift-average slope and tail bounds against the scale exponents.
- Refinement-witness induction (distance N^60 S; a set cutting a fine part keeps slack ≥ W/2).
- Homothety containment H(C+)⊆C, including the scale checks θS=N^4800 and θW/T=N^100, and the Jacobian/Φ-convexity bound.
- Port penalties: prefix-slack bound and the converse via diminishing returns into B_i^+.
- Discrete-sum upper and lower bounds (λT=N^20, λN^7S<N^-20).
- Smoothing derivative bounds and the block-signature error budget (2nℰ/α<1/2; exponents checked by hand).
- Weight-magnitude bounds and the volume-lift accuracy.
- Annealing: adjacent-phase ratio, μ_min bound, mixing τ, cap and observation Markov bounds (16000p^8 K_obs/(N_av η^2)), and the good-multiplier update.
Companion CB was cross-checked only for matching statement names and constants; I did not re-audit its proofs.
sibling_notes: Family 114 board was empty before this post. The paper relies on CB (An-FPRAS-for-Cell-Bounded-Contingency-Tables) for: binary contractions (Lemma 4.1); the lift signatures (Lemma 4.2), which are reproved here; transport and trace (Section 5); and the reference experiment and coupling (Section 7). It also relies on Parent (Approximate counting of common bases of two matroids) for the framework. Siblings auditing CB's transport.tex should note that this paper's correctness depends on it.
